slot.brief: Lens immersed in a medium of given refractive index; use lens-maker relation to find new focal length and nature of lens

stem: A concave lens made of glass ($\\mu = 1.5$) has a focal length of $10\\ \\text{cm}$ in air. When completely immersed in a liquid of refractive index $1.8$, it will behave as a:

verdicts.working: Lensmaker: 1/f = (μ_lens/μ_medium − 1)(1/R1 − 1/R2). In air: 1/(−10) = 0.5K → K = −0.2 cm⁻¹. In liquid: μ_rel = 1.5/1.8 = 5/6, so 1/f = (−1/6)(−0.2) = 1/30 → f = +30 cm, converging.

working:
According to the lens-maker's formula, the focal length of a lens in air is given by:
$$\frac{1}{f_a} = (\mu_g - 1)\left(\frac{1}{R_1} - \frac{1}{R_2}\right)$$
For a concave lens, $f_a = -10\ \text{cm}$.

When the lens is immersed in a liquid medium of refractive index $\mu_l$, its focal length $f_l$ is given by:
$$\frac{1}{f_l} = \left(\frac{\mu_g}{\mu_l} - 1\right)\left(\frac{1}{R_1} - \frac{1}{R_2}\right)$$

Taking the ratio of the two equations:
$$\frac{f_l}{f_a} = \frac{\mu_g - 1}{\dfrac{\mu_g}{\mu_l} - 1} = \frac{1.5 - 1}{\dfrac{1.5}{1.8} - 1} = \frac{0.5}{\dfrac{5}{6} - 1} = \frac{0.5}{-\dfrac{1}{6}} = -3$$

Therefore, the new focal length is:
$$f_l = -3 f_a = -3(-10\ \text{cm}) = +30\ \text{cm}$$

Since $f_l > 0$, the lens has a positive focal length, meaning it behaves as a converging lens of focal length $30\ \text{cm}$.

Independent check: Lensmaker: 1/f = (μ_lens/μ_medium − 1)(1/R1 − 1/R2). In air: 1/(−10) = 0.5K → K = −0.2 cm⁻¹. In liquid: μ_rel = 1.5/1.8 = 5/6, so 1/f = (−1/6)(−0.2) = 1/30 → f = +30 cm, converging.

draft.distractor_notes:
Option A encodes the error of computing the magnitude $|f_l| = 30\ \text{cm}$ correctly, but failing to recognize that the negative ratio inverts the diverging lens into a converging lens.
Option C encodes two errors: forgetting the factor of $(\mu_g - 1) = 0.5$ in the numerator (yielding $|f_l| = 6 \times 10 = 60\ \text{cm}$) and keeping the lens as diverging.
